module.Title: Create a Maintenance Report
module.Teaching: Loop through equipment records and use f-strings to create readable reports.
module.ExampleCode:
for fan in fans:
    print(f"{fan['name']}: {fan['hours']} hours")
module.TargetCode:
for pump in pumps:
    print(f"{pump['name']}: {pump['hours']} hours")
module.FillStarter:
for pump in pumps:
    print(f"{pump['___']}: {pump['___']} hours")
module.PredictionQuestion: Why use different quotation marks around dictionary keys?
PredictionOptions: To avoid ending the outer f-string
Python requires all keys to use single quotes
module.PredictionExplanation: Single quotes inside a double-quoted f-string avoid a quote collision.
module.BrokenCode:
for pump in pumps:
print(f"{pump["name"]}: {pump["hours"]} hours")
module.DebugPrompt: Indent the body and avoid conflicting quotation marks inside the f-string.
module.RecallPrompt: Rebuild the maintenance report loop. Use these exact identifiers: f, print, pump, pumps. Use the exact value "{pump['name']}: {pump['hours']} hours".
module.TransferPrompt: Report each fan's name and running state. Use these exact identifiers: f, fans, print. Use the exact value "{fan['name']}: Running = {fan['running']}".
module.TransferCode:
for fan in fans:
    print(f"{fan['name']}: Running = {fan['running']}")
module.PreviewMessage: The facility can now print readable maintenance information.
